feedback: The candidate matches the iteration 7 design exactly: kp 3.0, ki 1.0, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016, last_direction. That design raced in iteration 7 and scored 216.97, the best so far. Its oval finish rate was 4/20, s-bend progress 0.462 and slalom progress 0.1235. Iteration 8, which changed only ki to 1.2, scored 187.18, with oval finish rate 2/20 and s-bend steering_oscillation 0.339. The ki series (0.8 to 184.93, 1.0 to 216.97, 1.2 to 187.18) peaks near 1.0. Earlier races rule out wider outer sensors (iteration 3), higher kp (iteration 4) and lower base_speed (iteration 2). Approving this unchanged design gives the team its best known result, but it is a reproduction, not new information. Max_error stays near 0.06 m, which is still the open problem. After the race, if the score reproduces near 217, use the next revision round for one narrow test: base_speed 1.7 with everything else fixed, which may help oval finishes if completion_time stays well under 3 s. If the score falls well below 217, the seeds or simulator may differ from the earlier race, so re-check per-track progress before changing any field.
requested_changes: If the race reproduces about 217, test base_speed 1.7 with all other fields as in iteration 7. Iteration 2 showed that lowering base_speed to 1.2 removed oval finishes, so a small rise is the more plausible direction, and oval completion_time (1.93 s at 1.6) must stay well under 3.0 s.

Do not raise kd above 0.5 or ki above 1.0 without new evidence. Iteration 5 showed kd 0.5 raised s-bend progress, and iteration 8 showed ki 1.2 lowered the score, with s-bend oscillation near the 0.35 limit.
